name: circles_within_range
signature: circles_within_range(dist: float, positions: [float2], radiuses: [float], positions2: [float2], radiuses2: [float], gridsize: int2) -> [[int]]
description: Given a vector of 2D positions (and same size vectors of radiuses), returns a vector of vectors of indices (to the second set of positions and radiuses) of the circles that are within dist of eachothers radius. If the second set are [], the first set is used for both (and the self element is excluded). gridsize optionally specifies the size of the grid to use for accellerated lookup of nearby points. This is essential for the algorithm to be fast, too big or too small can cause slowdown. Omit it, and a heuristic will be chosen for you, which is currently sqrt(num_circles) * 2 along each dimension, e.g. 100 elements would use a 20x20 grid. Efficiency wise this algorithm is fastest if there is not too much variance in the radiuses of the second set and/or the second set has smaller radiuses than the first.

name: ensure_size
signature: ensure_size(string: string, size: int, char: int, extra: int = 0) -> string
description: ensures a string is at least size characters. if it is, just returns the existing string, otherwise returns it grown to that size (with optionally extra bytes added), with any new characters set to char: grown in place when the string has the room (see string_with_capacity), else as a new string of exactly that size. You can specify a negative size to mean relative to the end, i.e. new characters will be added at the start. Together with the write_ functions this lets a string be used as a byte buffer: those write into the string in place (visible thru every reference to it), except that a string constant is copied first, so a literal never changes.

name: write_int64_le
signature: write_int64_le(string: string, i: int, val: int) -> string, int
description: writes a value as little endian to a string at location i, in place, so the write is visible thru every reference to the string. A write past the end grows the string to end right after the value (bytes skipped over are 0): in place as well when the string has the room (see string_with_capacity), else as a new string with room to grow as much again, which is what a string that had to grow that way gets. Returns the string, which is the new one if it had to move or was a string constant (see ensure_size), and the index of the location right after where the value was written. The _back version writes relative to the end (and writes before the index), and grows the string to twice what it needs, with 0 bytes at the front, so what it wrote keeps its place from the end

name: gl.scale
description: scales the current coordinate system using a vector

name: gl.origin
description: returns a vector representing the current transform origin in pixels. only makes sense in 2D mode (no gl.perspective called).

name: gl.scaling
description: returns a vector representing the current transform scale in pixels. only makes sense in 2D mode (no gl.perspective called).

name: gl.model_view_projection
description: returns a vector representing the current model view projection matrix (16 elements)

name: gl.model_view
description: returns a vector representing the current model view matrix (16 elements)

name: gl.projection
description: returns a vector representing the current projection matrix (16 elements)

name: gl.push_model_view
description: save the current state of the model view matrix (gl.translate, gl.rotate etc)

name: gl.pop_model_view
description: restore a previous state of the model view matrix. returns false if none

name: gl.point_scale
description: sets the current scaling factor for point sprites. this can be what the current gl.scale is, or different, depending on the desired visuals. the ideal size may also be FOV dependent.

name: gl.line_mode
description: set line mode (true == on), returns previous mode

name: gl.cull_front
description: set culling front (true) or back (false), returns previous value.

name: gl.hit
description: whether the mouse/finger is inside of the rectangle specified in terms of the current transform (for touch screens only if the corresponding gl.isdown is true). Only true if the last rectangle for which gl.hit was true last frame is of the same size as this one (allows you to safely test in most cases of overlapping rendering)

name: gl.hit
description: whether the mouse/finger is inside of the rectangle specified in terms of the current transform (for touch screens only if the corresponding gl.isdown is true). Only true if the last rectangle for which gl.hit was true last frame is of the same size as this one (allows you to safely test in most cases of overlapping rendering)

name: gl.rect
description: renders a rectangle (0,0)..(1,1) (or (-1,-1)..(1,1) when centered), scaled by the given size.

name: gl.rect_tc_col
signature: gl.rect_tc_col(size: float2, tc: float2, tcsize: float2, cols: [float4])
description: Like gl.rect renders a sized quad, but allows you to specify texture coordinates and optionally colors (empty list for all white). Slow.

name: gl.unit_square
description: renders a square (0,0)..(1,1) (or (-1,-1)..(1,1) when centered)

name: gl.line
signature: gl.line(start: float2, end: float2, thickness: float)
description: renders a line with the given thickness

name: gl.line
signature: gl.line(start: float3, end: float3, thickness: float)
description: renders a line with the given thickness

name: gl.perspective
signature: gl.perspective(fovy: float, znear: float, zfar: float, frame_buffer_size: int2 = nil, frame_buffer_offset: int2 = nil, nodepth: int = 0)
description: changes from 2D mode (default) to 3D right handed perspective mode with vertical fov (try 60), far plane (furthest you want to be able to render, try 1000) and near plane (try 1). Optionally specify a framebuffer size to override the current gl.framebuffer_size

name: gl.ortho
description: changes back to 2D mode rendering with a coordinate system from (0,0) top-left to the screen size in pixels bottom right. this is the default at the start of a frame, use this call to get back to that after gl.perspective. Pass true to rh have (0,0) bottom-left instead. Pass true to depth to have depth testing/writing on.

name: gl.ortho3d
description: sets a custom ortho projection as 3D projection.

name: gl.new_poly
description: creates a mesh out of a loop of points, much like gl.polygon. gl.line_mode determines how this gets drawn (fan or loop). automatically generates texcoords and normals. returns mesh id

name: gl.new_mesh
signature: gl.new_mesh(format: string, positions: [float3], colors: [float4], normals: [float3], texcoords1: [float2], texcoords2: [float2], indices: [int] = nil) -> resource<mesh>
description: creates a new vertex buffer and returns an integer id (1..) for it. format must be made up of characters P (position), C (color), T (texcoord), N (normal). indices may be []. positions is obligatory. you may specify [] for any of the other attributes if not required by format, or to get defaults for colors (white) / texcoords (position x & y) / normals (generated from adjacent triangles).

name: gl.new_mesh_iqm
description: load a .iqm file into a mesh, returns mesh or nil on failure to load.

name: gl.mesh_parts
description: returns an array of names of all parts of mesh m (names may be empty)

name: gl.mesh_size
description: returns the number of verts in this mesh

name: gl.mesh_bounds
description: returns the min and max vert dimensions of this mesh

name: gl.mesh_animations
description: return names of animations

name: gl.mesh_animation_frames
signature: gl.mesh_animation_frames(m: resource<mesh>, name: string) -> int, int, float
description: given name, return animation's first frame, number of frames and framerate, or '-1, -1, 0.0' if name is invalid

name: gl.animate_mesh
description: set the frame for animated mesh m

name: gl.animate_mesh_blend
signature: gl.animate_mesh_blend(m: resource<mesh>, frame1: float, frame2: float, blending: float)
description: set the blending frames for animated mesh m

name: gl.render_mesh
description: renders the specified mesh

name: gl.save_mesh
signature: gl.save_mesh(m: resource<mesh>, name: string, format: int = 0) -> string?
description: saves the mesh to a file in the specified format (ply by default). for other supported formats, see modules/gl.lobster. warning: when using iqm format, make sure vertex format is 'PNC', which is being used by meshgen and cubegen. returns error string if any problems, nil otherwise.

name: gl.mesh_pointsize
description: sets the pointsize for this mesh. the mesh must have been created with indices = nil for point rendering to be used. you also want to use a shader that works with points, such as color_attr_particle.

name: gl.set_shader
description: changes the current shader. shaders must reside in the shaders folder, builtin ones are: color / textured / phong

name: gl.set_shader
description: changes the current shader from a value received from gl.get_shader

name: gl.get_shader
description: gets a shader by name, for use with gl.set_shader

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. size of the vector must match the size of the uniform in the shader. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. size of the vector must match the size of the uniform in the shader. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. size of the vector must match the size of the uniform in the shader. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. uniform in the shader must be a single float. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. size of the vector must match the size of the uniform in the shader. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. size of the vector must match the size of the uniform in the shader. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. size of the vector must match the size of the uniform in the shader. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform
description: set a uniform on the current shader. uniform in the shader must be a single int. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform_array
description: set a uniform on the current shader. uniform in the shader must be an array of vec4. returns false on error.

name: gl.set_uniform_matrix
signature: gl.set_uniform_matrix(name: string, value: [float], morerows: bool = false) -> int
description: set a uniform on the current shader. pass a vector of 4/6/9/12/16 floats to set a mat2/mat3x2/mat3/mat4x3/mat4 respectively. pass true for morerows to get mat2x3/mat3x4. returns false on error.

name: gl.update_buffer_object
signature: gl.update_buffer_object(value: string, ssbo: int, offset: int, existing: resource<bufferobject>, dyn: bool) -> resource<bufferobject>?
description: creates a uniform buffer object ssbo indicates if you want a shader storage block instead. returns buffer resource or nil on error.

name: gl.bind_buffer_object
description: attaches an existing bo to the current shader at the given uniform block name. uniforms in the shader can be any type, as long as it matches the data layout in the string buffer. returns false for error.

name: gl.copy_buffer_object
signature: gl.copy_buffer_object(source: resource<bufferobject>, destination: resource<bufferobject>, srcoffset: int, dstoffset: int, length: int)
description: copies the source buffer object into the destination buffer object

name: gl.bind_mesh_to_compute
description: Bind the vertex data of a mesh to a SSBO binding of a compute shader. Pass a nil mesh to unbind.

name: gl.dispatch_compute
description: dispatches the currently set compute shader in groups of sizes of the specified x/y/z values.

name: gl.auto_compute_barrier
description: whether a full memory barrier is issued after every dispatch_compute (default true). Apps that know their dependencies can turn this off and call gl.compute_barrier explicitly before each consumer instead, letting independent dispatches overlap.

name: gl.compute_barrier
description: makes imageStore/SSBO writes of preceding dispatches visible to subsequent commands. Only needed with gl.auto_compute_barrier(false).

name: gl.dump_shader
description: Dumps the compiled (binary) version of the current shader to a file. Contents are driver dependent. On Nvidia hardware it contains the assembly version of the shader as text, pass true for stripnonascii if you're only interested in that part.

name: gl.blend
description: changes the blending mode (use blending constants from texture.lobster), returns old mode

name: gl.load_texture
description: returns texture if succesfully loaded from file name, otherwise nil. see texture.lobster for texture format. If textureformat includes cubemap, will load 6 images with "_ft" etc inserted before the "." in the filename. Uses stb_image internally (see http://nothings.org/), loads JPEG Baseline, subsets of PNG, TGA, BMP, PSD, GIF, HDR, PIC.

name: gl.save_texture
signature: gl.save_texture(tex: resource<texture>, filename: string, flip: bool = false) -> int
description: saves the texture in .png format, returns true if succesful

name: gl.set_primitive_texture
signature: gl.set_primitive_texture(i: int, tex: resource<texture>, tf: int = 0)
description: sets texture unit i to texture (for use with rect/circle/polygon/line). if texture flags are given, sets those on the texture also

name: gl.set_mesh_texture
signature: gl.set_mesh_texture(mesh: resource<mesh>, part: int, i: int, texture: resource<texture>)
description: sets texture unit i to texture for a mesh and part (0 if not a multi-part mesh)

name: gl.set_image_texture
signature: gl.set_image_texture(i: int, tex: resource<texture>, level: int, accessflags: int = 0)
description: sets image unit i to texture (for use with compute). optionally specify writeonly/readwrite flags.

name: gl.unbind_all_textures
description: unbinds all textures set thru any set texture calls. typically not needed to call this manually, but may sometimes be needed when reusing textures across draw/compute calls

name: gl.create_texture
description: creates a texture from a 2d array of color vectors. see texture.lobster for texture format. for a cubemap, pass an array that is 6x as big on x than y

name: gl.create_texture_single_channel
description: creates a texture from a 2d array of float vectors. see texture.lobster for texture format. for a cubemap, pass an array that is 6x as big on x than y

name: gl.create_blank_texture
description: creates a blank texture (for use as frame buffer or with compute shaders). see texture.lobster for texture format

name: gl.create_colored_texture
signature: gl.create_colored_texture(size: int3, color: float4, textureformat: int = 0) -> resource<texture>
description: creates a colored texture (for use as frame buffer or with compute shaders). see texture.lobster for texture format

name: gl.texture_size
description: returns the size of a texture

name: gl.read_texture
description: read back RGBA texture data into a string or nil on failure

name: gl.generate_texture_mipmap
description: generate mipmaps for the specified texture

name: gl.switch_to_framebuffer
signature: gl.switch_to_framebuffer(tex: resource<texture> = nil, hasdepth: int = 0, multisampleformat: int = 0, resolvetex: resource<texture> = nil, depthtex: resource<texture> = nil) -> int
description: switches to a new framebuffer, that renders into the given texture. also allocates a depth buffer for it if depth is true. pass the multisample flags that was used for this texture. pass a resolve texture if the base texture is multisample. pass your own depth texture if desired. pass a nil texture to switch back to the original framebuffer. performance note: do not recreate texture passed in unless necessary.

name: gl.framebuffer_size
description: a vector representing the size (in pixels) of the framebuffer, according to the last call to gl.switch_to_framebuffer, or same as gl.window_size otherwise

name: gl.light
description: sets up a light at the given position for this frame. make sure to call this after your camera transforms but before any object transforms (i.e. defined in "worldspace"). params contains specular exponent in x (try 32/64/128 for different material looks) and the specular scale in y (try 1 for full intensity)

name: gl.render_tiles
signature: gl.render_tiles(positions: [float2], tilecoords: [int2], mapsize: int2, sizes: [float], rotations: [float])
description: Renders a list of tiles from a tilemap. Each tile rendered is 0.5 in radius (1x1 square around pos) unless the optional sizes vector is specified (may be empty). Positions may be anywhere. tilecoords are indices into the map (0..mapsize-1), mapsize is the amount of tiles in the texture. rotations are optional (may be empty, faster if not specified). Tiles may overlap, they are drawn in order. Before calling this, make sure to have the texture set and a textured shader. If you want tile to use top-left as position, wrap this call in gl.translate float2_h:

name: gl.debug_grid
signature: gl.debug_grid(num: int3, dist: float3, thickness: float)
description: renders a grid in space for debugging purposes. num is the number of lines in all 3 directions, and dist their spacing. thickness of the lines in the same units

name: gl.screenshot
signature: gl.screenshot(filename: string, resolution: int2 = nil) -> int
description: saves a screenshot in .png format, returns true if succesful. resolution optionally gives a target size to resize the screenshot to; (0,0) or the current window size means no resizing

name: gl.get_renderer_info_string
description: Get a string describing the renderer, typically OpenGL vendor - renderer - version

name: gl.dropped_file
description: if a file was dropped on the window this frame, the filename, otherwise empty

name: gl.create_time_query
description: creates a time query object used for profiling GPU events

name: gl.start_time_query
description: starts the time query

name: gl.stop_time_query
description: stops the time query and returns the result

name: gl.init_controller_database
description: loads the controller database if you want your game to support controllers. typically the argument should be: pakfile "data/controllers/gamecontrollerdb.txt". returns error if something went wrong

name: gl.open_url
description: Opens a URL in the system browser, returns true if successful

name: gl.set_clipboard
description: Set the contents of the system clipboard

name: gl.get_clipboard
description: Get the contents of the system clipboard

name: gl.set_font_name
description: sets a freetype/OTF/TTF font as current (and loads it from disk the first time). returns true if success.

name: gl.set_font_size
signature: gl.set_font_size(size: int, outlinesize: float = 0.000000, outlinecolor: float4 = nil) -> int
description: sets the font for rendering into this fontsize (in pixels). caches into a texture first time this size is used, flushes from cache if this size is not used an entire frame. font rendering will look best if using 1:1 pixels (careful with gl.scale/gl.translate). an optional outlinesize will give the font an outline. make sure to call this every frame. returns true if success

name: gl.set_max_font_size
description: sets the max font size to render to bitmaps. any sizes specified over that by setfontsize will still work but cause scaled rendering. default 256

name: gl.get_font_size
description: the current font size

name: gl.get_outline_size
description: the current font size

name: gl.text
description: renders a text with the current font (at the current coordinate origin)

name: gl.text_size
description: the x/y size in pixels the given text would need

name: gl.get_glyph_name
description: the name of a glyph index, or empty string if the font doesn't have names

name: gl.get_char_code
description: the char code of a glyph by specifying its name, or 0 if it can not be found (or if the font doesn't have names)

name: gl.use_default_font_shader
description: by default set_font_name sets the use of the "textured" shader. With this function you can turn that on/off to use a current shader instead.

name: play_wav
signature: play_wav(filename: string, loops: int = 0, prio: int = 0) -> int
description: plays a sound defined by a wav file (RAW or MS-ADPCM, any bitrate other than 22050hz 16bit will automatically be converted on first load). the default volume is the max volume (1.0) loops is the number of repeats to play (-1 repeats endlessly, omit for no repeats). prio is the priority of the sound which determines whether it can be deleted or not in case of too many play function calls (defaults to 0) returns the assigned channel number (1..8) or 0 on error

name: load_wav
description: loads a sound the same way play_sound does, but ahead of playback, to avoid any delays later. returns false on error

name: play_sfxr
signature: play_sfxr(filename: string, loops: int = 0, prio: int = 0) -> int
description: plays a synth sound defined by a .sfs file (use http://www.drpetter.se/project_sfxr.html to generate these). the default volume is the max volume (1.0) loops is the number of repeats to play (-1 repeats endlessly, omit for no repeats). prio is the priority of the sound which determines whether it can be deleted or not in case of too many play function calls (defaults to 0) returns the assigned channel number (1..8) or 0 on error

name: load_sfxr
description: loads a sound the same way play_sfxr does, but ahead of playback, to avoid any delays later. returns false on error

name: play_ogg
signature: play_ogg(filename: string, loops: int = 0, prio: int = 0) -> int
description: plays an ogg file. the default volume is the max volume (1.0) loops is the number of repeats to play (-1 repeats endlessly, omit for no repeats). prio is the priority of the sound which determines whether it can be deleted or not in case of too many play function calls (defaults to 0) returns the assigned channel number (1..8) or 0 on error

name: load_ogg
description: loads a sound the same way play_ogg does, but ahead of playback, to avoid any delays later. returns false on error

name: play_audio_stream
signature: play_audio_stream(freq: int, channels: int, prio: int = 0) -> int
description: plays an audio stream which can be filled via put_audio_stream(). the default volume is the max volume (1.0) prio is the priority of the sound which determines whether it can be deleted or not in case of too many play function calls (defaults to 0) returns the assigned channel number (1..8) or 0 on error

name: put_audio_stream
description: puts audio samples in range [-1.0,1.0] into an audio stream created with play_audio_stream().

name: has_audio_stream
description: returns whether the given channel has an audio stream

name: audio_stream_available
description: returns the number of samples available in the audio stream

name: sound_status
description: provides the status of the specified sound channel. returns -1 on error or if the channel does not exist, 0 if the channel is free, 1 if it is playing, and 2 if the channel is active but paused.

name: sound_halt
description: terminates a specific sound channel.

name: sound_pause
description: pauses the specified sound channel.

name: sound_resume
description: resumes a sound that was paused.

name: sound_volume
description: sets the channel volume in the range 0..1.

name: sound_position
signature: sound_position(channel: int, vecfromlistener: float3, listenerfwd: float3, attnscale: float)
description: sets the channel volume and panning according to sound in a game world relative to the listener.

name: sound_no_position
description: clears the channel position previously set by "sound_position"

name: sound_time_length
description: returns the length in seconds of the sound playing on this channel

name: text_to_speech
description: Queues up text for async text to speech output. Currently on: win32

name: text_to_speech_stop
description: Stops current text to speech output and clears queue

name: play_music
description: plays music in many common formats (WAV, MP3, OGG, etc.). the default volume is the max volume (1.0) loops is the number of repeats to play (-1 repeats endlessly, omit for no repeats). returns the music id or 0 on error

name: play_music_fade_in
signature: play_music_fade_in(filename: string, ms: int, loops: int = 0) -> int
description: plays music while fading in over ms milliseconds. See play_music for more info.

name: play_music_cross_fade
signature: play_music_cross_fade(old_mus_id: int, new_filename: string, ms: int, loops: int = 0) -> int
description: cross-fades new music with existing music over ms milliseconds. See play_music for more info.

name: music_fade_out
description: fade out music over ms milliseconds.

name: music_halt
description: stop music with the given id.

name: music_pause
description: pause music with the given id.

name: music_resume
description: resume music with the given id.

name: music_volume
description: set the music volume in the range 0..1.

name: music_is_playing
description: returns whether the music with the given id has not yet finished. Paused music is still considered to be playing

name: music_set_general_volume
description: set the general music volume in the range 0..1.

name: mic_devices
description: returns the available microphone devices as two lists: their ids (used with mic_start) and their names

name: mic_start
description: start recording audio from the given device id, at the given frequency. Returns a mic_id.

name: mic_stop
description: stop recording. Returns false if the mic_id is invalid

name: mic_get
description: gets audio sample data in float format from the given microphone device.

name: ph.initialize
description: initializes or resets the physical world, gravity typically [0, -10].

name: ph.create_box
signature: ph.create_box(position: float2, size: float2, offset: float2 = nil, rotation: float = 0.000000, attachto: resource<fixture> = nil) -> resource<fixture>
description: creates a physical box shape in the world at position, with size the half-extends around the center, offset from the center if needed, at a particular rotation (in degrees). attachto is a previous physical object to attach this one to, to become a combined physical body.

name: ph.create_circle
signature: ph.create_circle(position: float2, radius: float, offset: float2 = nil, attachto: resource<fixture> = nil) -> resource<fixture>
description: creates a physical circle shape in the world at position, with the given radius, offset from the center if needed. attachto is a previous physical object to attach this one to, to become a combined physical body.

name: ph.create_polygon
signature: ph.create_polygon(position: float2, vertices: [float2], attachto: resource<fixture> = nil) -> resource<fixture>
description: creates a polygon circle shape in the world at position, with the given list of vertices. attachto is a previous physical object to attach this one to, to become a combined physical body.

name: ph.dynamic
description: makes a shape dynamic (on = true) or not.

name: ph.set_linear_velocity
description: sets the linear velocity of a shape's center of mass.

name: ph.apply_linear_impulse_to_center
description: applies a linear impulse to a shape at its center of mass.

name: ph.set_color
description: sets a shape (or nil for particles) to be rendered with a particular color.

name: ph.set_shader
description: sets a shape (or nil for particles) to be rendered with a particular shader.

name: ph.set_texture
signature: ph.set_texture(id: resource<fixture>, tex: resource<texture>, texunit: int = 0)
description: sets a shape (or nil for particles) to be rendered with a particular texture (assigned to a texture unit, default 0).

name: ph.get_position
description: gets a shape's position.

name: ph.get_mass
description: gets a shape's mass.

name: ph.create_particle
signature: ph.create_particle(position: float2, velocity: float2, color: float4, flags: int = 0) -> int
description: creates an individual particle. For flags, see include/physics.lobster

name: ph.create_particle_circle
signature: ph.create_particle_circle(position: float2, radius: float, color: float4, flags: int = 0)
description: creates a circle filled with particles. For flags, see include/physics.lobster

name: ph.initialize_particles
description: initializes the particle system with a given particle radius.

name: ph.step
signature: ph.step(seconds: float, viter: int, piter: int)
description: simulates the physical world for the given period (try: gl.delta_time()). You can specify the amount of velocity/position iterations per step, more means more accurate but also more expensive computationally (try 8 and 3).

name: ph.particle_contacts
description: gets the particle indices that are currently contacting a giving physics object. Call after step(). Indices may be invalid after next step().

name: ph.raycast
signature: ph.raycast(p1: float2, p2: float2, n: int) -> [int]
description: returns a vector of the first n particle ids that intersect a ray from p1 to p2, not including particles that overlap p1.

name: ph.delete_particle
description: deletes given particle. Deleting particles causes indices to be invalidated at next step().

name: ph.getparticle_position
description: gets a particle's position, or 0 if there is no such particle.

name: ph.render
description: renders all rigid body objects.

name: ph.render_particles
description: render all particles, with the given scale.

name: mg.sphere
description: a sphere

name: mg.cube
description: a cube (extents are size from center)

name: mg.cylinder
description: a unit cylinder (height is from center)

name: mg.tapered_cylinder
signature: mg.tapered_cylinder(bot: float, top: float, height: float)
description: a cyclinder where you specify the top and bottom radius (height is from center)

name: mg.superquadric
description: a super quadric. specify an exponent of 2 for spherical, higher values for rounded squares

name: mg.superquadric_non_uniform
signature: mg.superquadric_non_uniform(posexponents: float3, negexponents: float3, posscale: float3, negscale: float3)
description: a superquadric that allows you to specify exponents and sizes in all 6 directions independently for maximum modelling possibilities

name: mg.supertoroid
description: a super toroid. R is the distance from the origin to the center of the ring.

name: mg.landscape
description: a simplex landscape of unit size

name: mg.set_polygon_reduction
description: controls the polygon reduction algorithm. set polyreductionpasses to 0 for off, 100 for max compression, or low values for generation speed or to keep the mesh uniform. epsilon determines how flat adjacent triangles must be to be reduced, use 0.98 as a good tradeoff, lower to get more compression. maxtricornerdot avoid very thin triangles, use 0.95 as a good tradeoff, up to 0.99 to get more compression

name: mg.set_color_noise
description: applies simplex noise to the colors of the model. try 0.3 for intensity. stretch scales the pattern over the model

name: mg.set_vertex_randomize
description: randomizes all verts produced to give a more organic look and to hide the inherent messy polygons produced by the algorithm. try 0.15. note that any setting other than 0 will likely counteract the polygon reduction algorithm

name: mg.set_point_mode
description: generates a point mesh instead of polygons

name: mg.polygonize
description: returns a generated mesh from past mg commands. subdiv determines detail and number of polygons (relative to the largest dimension of the model), try 30.. 300 depending on the subject. values much higher than that will likely make you run out of memory (or take very long).

name: mg.convert_to_cubes
description: returns a cubegen block (see cg_ functions) from past mg commands. subdiv determines detail and number of cubes (relative to the largest dimension of the model).

name: mg.translate
description: translates the current coordinate system along a vector

name: mg.scale
description: scales the current coordinate system by the given factor

name: mg.scale_vec
description: non-unimformly scales the current coordinate system using individual factors per axis

name: mg.rotate
description: rotates using axis/angle

name: mg.color
description: sets the color, where an alpha of 1 means to add shapes to the scene (union), and 0 substracts them (carves)

name: mg.smooth
description: sets the smoothness in terms of the range of distance from the shape smoothing happens, defaults to 1.0

name: mg.push_transform
description: save the current state of the transform

name: mg.pop_transform
description: restore a previous state of the transform

name: steam.workshop_sync
description: makes subscribed workshop content progress towards being downloaded, and copies each item's files into dest_dir (relative to the main write dir, or absolute) once its download completes. If own_subdirs is true, each item's files go into a subdirectory of dest_dir named after its workshop file id, otherwise all items' files are copied into dest_dir together. Files keep the names they were uploaded with either way (so with own_subdirs false, identically named files from different items overwrite each other). Call this regularly (e.g. once per frame, needs steam.update()) while you want content to come in. Returns a status: -1 = error copying files, 0 = all subscribed content is installed and copied (nothing left to do), 1 = downloads still in progress, 2 = done but some items failed to download. Second return value is the files copied by this call (full paths), so the game can pick up new/updated content the moment it arrives.

name: steam.workshop_upload_start
signature: steam.workshop_upload_start(content_folder: string, title: string, description: string, metadata: string, changenote: string, preview_image: string, existing_fileid: int) -> int
description: starts uploading workshop content for the current app; this is async, poll workshop_upload_status() (with steam.update() running) for the result. content_folder (relative to the main write dir, or absolute) must contain exactly the file(s) making up this single workshop item, e.g. a staging folder the level editor saved the level file into; the original filenames inside it are preserved for downloaders (see workshop_sync()). title and description are user visible on the workshop. metadata is NOT user visible and may be empty; use it to store things the game may want to query later without downloading, e.g. the original filename or version info (max 5000 chars). changenote may be empty. preview_image optionally (empty = none) points to a jpg/png/gif under 1MB shown on the workshop page. Pass 0 as existing_fileid to publish a NEW item, or the file id of previously uploaded content to update it; an update first verifies the item is owned by the current steam user and fails otherwise (status -2). On a successful new upload, the game MUST store the file id returned by workshop_upload_status() alongside the content (e.g. in the level file or its own sidecar/registry) and pass it back in here when the user uploads a new version of the same content, since steam has no other way to know it's the same item. Empty title/description/metadata leave the existing values unchanged when updating. Returns false if the upload could not be started (e.g. one is already in progress).

name: steam.workshop_upload_status
signature: steam.workshop_upload_status() -> int, int, int, int, int
description: gets the status of the upload started with workshop_upload_start(): 0 = no upload started, 1 = in progress, 2 = done succesfully, -1 = failed, -2 = failed because the existing item is owned by a different steam user. Further return values are: the workshop file id (once known, 0 before; on success the game must store this with the content, see workshop_upload_start()), whether the user still needs to accept the steam workshop legal agreement (if true, the item remains hidden until they do; send them there with workshop_open_legal_agreement() or workshop_open_item_page()), and upload progress as bytes processed and bytes total (both may be 0 in early stages).

description: creates a UI for any lobster reference value, and returns the edited version

name: im.show_vars
description: shows an automatic editing UI for each global variable in your program

name: breakpoint
description: stops the program in the debugger if passed true. debugger needs --runtime-stack-trace on, and im.init() to have run.

name: breakpoint
description: stops the program in the debugger always. debugger needs --runtime-stack-trace on, and im.init() to have run.

name: write_debug_dump
description: writes a .flex file at this point. needs --runtime-stack-trace on.
